---
title: "Diet indices vs alpha diversity"
author: "Giacomo Antonello"
format: html
params:
  outdir: "results/alpha_diversity"
---

**Overall hypothesis**: The oral microbiome modifies health outcomes given by a diet
pattern.

**Microbiome hypothesis**: Worse eating habits affect oral microbiome, maybe nitrate or acid
producing bacteria. Worse eating habits are:

  - Lower Healthy Eating Index (HEI)
  - Higher Ultraprocessed foods index (NOVA)

**Model**, for each alpha diversity metric and each diet index:

`alpha ~ diet index + covariates`

# Survey weighting

**Decision**: the primary models are survey-weighted; unweighted models are
reported as a sensitivity analysis.

**Why weight.** The NHANES oral microbiome documentation (`OralMicrobiomeDataDocumentation-508.pdf`)
states that analyses should use the survey design variables and sample weights.
NHANES is a multistage cluster sample, which has two consequences for unweighted models:

  1. **Standard errors are too small.** Participants in the same primary sampling
     unit (PSU) are more alike than independent observations. Design-based variance
     uses strata (`SDMVSTRA`) and PSUs (`SDMVPSU`), and its degrees of freedom
     are the number of PSUs minus the number of strata, not the number of participants.
  2. **Estimates describe the sample, not the population.** NHANES oversamples
     some groups (e.g. Black, Hispanic, Asian, low-income, and older participants).
     Weights give estimates for US civilian non-institutionalized adults aged 20-69,
     which matters if the diet-microbiome association differs across these groups.

Weighting is also consistent with the companion MaPiDS-mortality paper, which uses
survey-weighted Cox models.

**Weight.** The documentation recommends examination weights, but the exposures
are 24-hour dietary recalls, so the dietary day-1 weight is used (`WTDRD1`, the
most restrictive subsample in the analysis), divided by 2 to combine the 2009-2010
and 2011-2012 cycles.

**Subpopulation.** The design is built on all NHANES 2009-2012 participants and
then restricted to each model's analytic sample with `subset()`, so that variance
is estimated correctly for a subpopulation (dropping participants before building
the design would understate the standard errors).

**Costs.** Weighted estimates are less precise (wider confidence intervals).
Community-level methods (PERMANOVA, betadisper, Dirichlet Multinomial Mixtures)
have no standard design-based versions, so those analyses are run unweighted, with
permutations restricted within strata and adjustment for the oversampling variables
(age, race/ethnicity, income), which are already covariates here.

Set `use_survey_weights <- FALSE` in the Variables chunk to run unweighted models only.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(survey)
library(haven)
library(broom)
library(openxlsx2)

theme_set(theme_light(base_size = 14))
dir.create(params$outdir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

load("../NHANES_oral_microbiome.se.rda")
```

# Variables

Edit the vectors below to change the analysis. To drop a covariate, delete
(or comment out) its line in `covariates`; everything downstream adapts.

```{r variables}
# outcomes
alpha_indices <- c(
  "Observed richness" = "alpha_Observed",
  "Shannon diversity" = "alpha_Shannon",
  "Faith's phylogenetic diversity" = "alpha_Faith"
)

# exposures. TODO: add MaPiDS when available
diet_indices <- c(
  "HEI-2020" = "HEI2020_ALL",
  "UPF (% calories)" = "nova4_propcal",
  "UPF (% grams)" = "nova4_propg"
)

# adjustment set
covariates <- c(
  "age",                # years
  "sex",
  "raceth",             # race/ethnicity
  "edu",                # education
  "pir",                # family income to poverty ratio
  "smoke_status",
  "alcohol_cat",
  "bmi",
  "kcal",               # total energy intake
  "OH_n_natural_teeth", # number of natural teeth
  "cycle"               # NHANES cycle, 2009-2010 or 2011-2012
)

# reference levels of categorical covariates
reference_levels <- list(
  sex = "Female",
  raceth = "Non_Hispanic_White",
  edu = "College_or_Above",
  smoke_status = "Never",
  alcohol_cat = "No_12plus_drinks",
  cycle = "2009-2010"
)

# FALSE fits unweighted models only (see Survey weighting)
use_survey_weights <- TRUE
```

```{r prepare data}
metadata.df <- data.frame(colData(NHANES_oral_microbiome.se))

# character covariates to factors with the chosen reference level
for (covariate in intersect(names(reference_levels), covariates)) {
  metadata.df[[covariate]] <- relevel(factor(metadata.df[[covariate]]), ref = reference_levels[[covariate]])
}
```

```{r survey design}
# design variables and dietary day-1 weights for all NHANES 2009-2012 participants
nhanes_design.df <- bind_rows(
  read_xpt("../../2009-2010/DEMO_F.xpt") %>%
    left_join(read_xpt("../../2009-2010/DR1TOT_F_diet.xpt") %>% select(SEQN, WTDRD1), by = "SEQN"),
  read_xpt("../../2011-2012/DEMO_G_demo.xpt") %>%
    left_join(read_xpt("../../2011-2012/DR1TOT_G_diet.xpt") %>% select(SEQN, WTDRD1), by = "SEQN")
) %>%
  transmute(
    SEQN = as.character(SEQN),
    SDMVPSU, SDMVSTRA,
    # 2 cycles combined; no dietary recall means weight 0
    wt_diet1_full = replace_na(WTDRD1, 0) / 2
  )

nhanes_full.svy <- svydesign(
  ids = ~ SDMVPSU,
  strata = ~ SDMVSTRA,
  weights = ~ wt_diet1_full,
  nest = TRUE,
  data = nhanes_design.df
)
```

# Models

Diet indices are standardized (mean 0, SD 1) within each analytic sample, so
estimates are the change in alpha diversity per 1 SD of the index and are
comparable across indices. Each model uses complete cases for its own outcome,
index, and covariates.

```{r fit models}
# single place where the model is fit: swap this out to change the method
fit_model <- function(formula, data, weighted) {
  if (!weighted) return(lm(formula, data = data))

  # restrict the full design to the analytic sample, then add the analysis variables
  model.svy <- subset(nhanes_full.svy, SEQN %in% data$SEQN)
  model.svy$variables <- left_join(model.svy$variables, data, by = "SEQN")
  svyglm(formula, design = model.svy)
}

model_methods <- c("Survey-weighted" = TRUE, "Unweighted" = FALSE)
if (!use_survey_weights) model_methods <- model_methods["Unweighted"]

alpha_models.df <- expand_grid(alpha = alpha_indices, diet = diet_indices, weighted = model_methods) %>%
  mutate(
    data = map2(alpha, diet, \(a, d) metadata.df %>%
                  select(SEQN, all_of(c(a, d, covariates))) %>%
                  drop_na() %>%
                  mutate(across(all_of(d), \(x) as.numeric(scale(x))))),
    formula = map2(alpha, diet, \(a, d) reformulate(c(d, covariates), response = a)),
    model = pmap(list(formula, data, weighted), fit_model),
    n = map_int(data, nrow)
  )

# split model terms into variable and level, e.g. "racethMexican_American" into
# "raceth" and "Mexican_American"; continuous variables have no level
term_variable <- function(term, variables) {
  matches <- variables[startsWith(term, variables)]
  matches[which.max(nchar(matches))]
}

# all terms except the intercept, for the diet index and the covariates
alpha_all_terms.df <- alpha_models.df %>%
  mutate(
    method = names(model_methods)[match(weighted, model_methods)],
    tidy = map(model, \(m) tidy(m, conf.int = TRUE) %>% filter(term != "(Intercept)"))
  ) %>%
  select(method, alpha, diet, n, tidy) %>%
  unnest(tidy) %>%
  mutate(
    alpha_label = names(alpha_indices)[match(alpha, alpha_indices)],
    diet_label = names(diet_indices)[match(diet, diet_indices)],
    term_type = ifelse(term == diet, "diet index", "covariate"),
    variable = map2_chr(term, diet, \(t, d) term_variable(t, c(d, covariates))),
    level = na_if(str_remove(term, fixed(variable)), ""),
    .after = diet
  ) %>%
  # FDR within each alpha diversity metric and method, across diet index models and terms
  group_by(alpha, method) %>%
  mutate(p.adj = p.adjust(p.value, method = "BH")) %>%
  ungroup()

# diet index terms only, for the summary table and the forest plot
alpha_results.df <- alpha_all_terms.df %>%
  filter(term_type == "diet index")

alpha_results.df %>%
  select(method, alpha_label, diet_label, n, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value, p.adj) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

```{r forest plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
alpha_forest_plot <- ggplot(alpha_results.df, aes(x = estimate, y = diet_label, color = method)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high), position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  facet_wrap(~ alpha_label, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_color_brewer(type = "qual", palette = "Set1") +
  labs(
    x = "Change in alpha diversity per 1 SD of the diet index (95% CI)",
    y = "",
    color = ""
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

alpha_forest_plot
```

# Write results

One sheet per alpha diversity metric, with all model terms (diet index and
covariates). `p.adj` is the Benjamini-Hochberg FDR within each sheet and method.
For categorical covariates, `level` is compared with the reference level set in
`reference_levels`.

```{r write results}
alpha_all_terms.df %>%
  arrange(method, diet_label, desc(term_type == "diet index"), str_to_lower(variable), level) %>%
  select(method, diet_label, term_type, variable, level, n, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, statistic, p.value, p.adj, alpha_label) %>%
  split(.$alpha_label) %>%
  map(\(x) select(x, -alpha_label)) %>%
  write_xlsx(file = file.path(params$outdir, "alpha_vs_diet_indices.xlsx"))
ggsave(plot = alpha_forest_plot, filename = file.path(params$outdir, "alpha_vs_diet_forest_plot.svg"), height = 4, width = 10)
```
